name: Semantic search and RAG
needs: find documents by meaning, not exact words
let users chat with their own documents
the AI should answer from my help articles
summary: Turning text into embeddings (lists of numbers that capture meaning) so you can find passages similar to a question even when the words differ. RAG feeds the best passages to a model so it answers from your content instead of guessing.
need_when: Users ask questions in their own words, or an AI feature must answer from your documents.
skip_when: Users search for names, codes or exact phrases. Full-text search does that better and cheaper.

ways.title: pgvector in Postgres
ways.how: Store chunk embeddings in a vector column with an HNSW index next to your data, and filter by owner in the same query.
ways.tradeoff: One database, normal permissions and backups. Tuning is up to you at large scale.

ways.title: Hybrid search
ways.how: Run full-text and vector search together and merge the results (for example reciprocal rank fusion). Meilisearch and Typesense support hybrid search too.
ways.tradeoff: Catches both exact terms and meaning. A bit more logic to maintain.

ways.title: A managed vector database
ways.how: Pinecone, Qdrant Cloud or Weaviate Cloud, or your AI provider's file search tool.
ways.tradeoff: Scales without tuning. Another copy of your data to keep in sync and secure.

prompt:
Add semantic search (and answers from it) over [documents] in this app.

Requirements:
- Split documents into chunks of about [500] tokens with some overlap, keeping the title and section heading with each chunk.
- Create embeddings with [embedding model] in a background job on create and update. Store them with pgvector and an HNSW index, plus the owner or tenant id.
- Every search query filters by the current user's access before ranking.
- Combine vector and full-text results, and return the top [5] chunks with links to their source.
- For answers, send only those chunks to the model, tell it to answer only from them and say when it doesn't know, and show the sources.
- Re-embed when a document changes and delete chunks when it's deleted.
- Build a test set of 20 questions with known source documents and report how often the right source is in the top 5.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. A question using different words from the document still finds it.
2. User B's question never retrieves user A's chunks.
3. Deleting a document removes it from results and answers.
4. Answers cite their sources, and a question with no answer in the docs gets 'I don't know'.
5. The right source is in the top 5 for at least [18 of 20] test questions.
acceptance_checks: A question using different words from the document still finds it.
User B's question never retrieves user A's chunks.
Deleting a document removes it from results and answers.
Answers cite their sources, and a question with no answer in the docs gets 'I don't know'.
The right source is in the top 5 for at least [18 of 20] test questions.
if_you_skip_it: Answers made up from nowhere, results from other users' documents, and stale answers from deleted files.
